successors.name: Portuguese Angola
successors.text: Matamba as it stood after the treaty of 7 September 1683: Malanje Province without the Lukala side (Ndongo's) and without the Kwango band (Kasanje's)

ledger.x: 1530: Matamba first appears in the record.
1620: Kasanje takes ground that Matamba claims.
1631: Nzinga conquers Matamba and joins it to Ndongo.
1683 September: the treaty ends the claim.
1683 September: Matamba becomes a nominal Portuguese vassal.
1836: the kingdom of Matamba ends in the Portuguese conquest.

wars.name: Nzinga's wars against Portugal (Matamba as her base)
wars.outcome: From Matamba Nzinga rebuilt her army, reclaimed large parts of Ndongo in 1641-1644, routed a Portuguese army at Kombi in 1647 and made peace in late 1656.

wars.name: Matamba-Kasanje wars (1620 attack, Nzinga 1634-35, Francisco 1681)
wars.outcome: Kasanje's Imbangala band attacked Matamba in the late 1610s-1620, Njinga made several wars against Kasanje especially in 1634-5, Francisco was involved in a war with Kasanje in 1681, and the treaty of 7 September 1683 made Matamba acknowledge Kasanje's…

wars.name: Battle of Katole and the treaty of 1683
wars.outcome: Francisco attacked at dawn at Katole on 4 September 1681 (a Portuguese tactical victory, the Battle of Katole page); the treaty of 7 September 1683 made Verónica a nominal vassal of Portugal.

wars.name: Portuguese invasion of Matamba (1744)
wars.outcome: Ana II faced a Portuguese invasion and signed a treaty of vassalage that renewed the points of 1683 and had little effect on the real sovereignty of Matamba.

certainty.note: No boundary is given by any page; Matamba is placed by a Malanje Province proxy (confidence 1-2).
